strategies.desc: Direct translation of the reference: 8 iterations each containing one all_reduce, forward bidiagonal coupling, backward decoupling, and division operations. 8 all_reduce dispatches total. Represents the baseline with maximum clarity but no fusion optimizations.

strategies.name: Fused Coupling-Decoupling Local Operations
strategies.desc: Same 8 all_reduce dispatches, but fuse all local tensor operations (coupling, decoupling, division) between consecutive all_reduces into single kernel launches per stage. Reduces local compute dispatches from ~32 to ~8 while keeping communication cost identical, trading off kernel complexity for dispatch overhead.

strategies.name: Pipelined Reduce-Scatter All-Gather Chain
strategies.desc: Replace each all_reduce with reduce_scatter followed by all_gather, allowing overlap of the 224 shards' communication. Each of 8 stages becomes 2 collectives (16 total), but with smaller per-rank payloads (2048 vs 458752 elements) that may saturate bandwidth better and enable better pipelining across stages.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Exploit potential node structure by performing intra-node all_reduce followed by inter-node all_reduce at each stage, assuming multi-node deployment. 16 total collectives (8 stages × 2 levels), but smaller within-node groups may use faster NVLink/ICI while inter-node uses network, potentially reducing critical path latency.

strategies.name: Broadcast-Reduce with Persistent Buffer
strategies.desc:
Instead of all_reduce, decompose into all_to_all or series of broadcast operations to distribute shards, then perform local bidiagonal operations on each rank's received data, followed by reduce to accumulate. Trades 8 all_reduce for potentially 8×2 point-to-point collective patterns, beneficial if all_reduce has poor scaling at world_size=224.
